(grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf. · also + aor. subj., ’before’ (πρὶν … ἐπέλθῃ ’before it comes upon’) · also + opt.: ’before’ (πρὶν τλαίη ’before he would bring himself’) · also adv. with a finite verb, ’before that, sooner’ (πρὶν … ἀγείρετο ’before that … came gathering’) · also + fut. indic.: ’before’ (πρὶν … γαῖα καθέξει ’before the earth covers’)

πόλινδε: πόλις — city; acc. sg. + suffix -δε ’towards’: ’to the city’
πᾶσι: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl.
πῆμα: πῆμα — woe, calamity, disaster; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg., direct object: ’woe’

σέ: σύ — you (sg.); acc. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’you’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’)
στήθεσσιν: στῆθος — breast, chest; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι(ν) (= Attic στήθεσι)
σταθμῷ: σταθμός — steading, farm-building, stall; masc. dat. sg.
στενάχοντες: στενάχω — groan, lament; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., epic (= στένω): ’groaning’
στῆθος: στῆθος — breast, chest; neut. acc. sg.
συβῶτα: συβώτης — swineherd; masc. voc. sg., epic -α (in apposition to Εὔμαιε)
σφιν: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. dat. pl./sg. pron.: ’to/for them’
σύες: σῦς (ὗς) — swine, pig; masc./fem. nom. pl.
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also as adverb, ’together’, or as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: σὺν … κάλυψε = συνεκάλυψε ’covered up’; σὺν … ἔπεσον = συνέπεσον ’fell together, clashed’ · also adverb ’along, with (us)’ construed with ἔχοντες, which takes the object (σὺν … χεῖρας ἔχοντες ’having hands along with us’)
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’
τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.; also relative: ’which’ (accented τά before a following enclitic)
τάς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. pl.: ’them’, of the Sirens · also ’them’, of the rocks (accented before the enclitic γε)
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι) · adj. · also plain interrogative, direct object/predicate: ’what’ (τί πάθω ’what am I to suffer’; τί ... γένηται ’what is to become’) · also the enclitic indefinite as an adjective agreeing with a noun, accented before enclitic που: εἴ τί που εἴλυμα ’if any wrapper’ · also enclitic indefinite with a negative, ’anything’, as accusative subject of an infinitive (οὐ … τί φημι κακώτερον ἄλλο … συγχεῦαι ’I say nothing else is worse’) · also enclitic indefinite, adverbial without a negative: ’somehow, in some way’ (τοῦτό τί μοι κάλλιστον ’this seems to me somehow the fairest’) · also enclitic indefinite as an adjective after μή, accented before an enclitic: ’any’ (μή τί τοι … πῆμα ’any harm to you’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ὅπως, accented before enclitic μοι: ’any’ (τί … ἄλγος ’any pain’)
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
ταῦτα: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τετυκοίμεθα: τεύχω — make, prepare; aor. opt. mid. 1 pl., epic reduplicated aorist (τετυκ-): ’we might prepare’
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’) · also ὅ τι as an adverbial acc. in an indirect question: ’why’ · also as a substantive object in a statement: ’something’ (καί τι ἴσασι ’they know something’)
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιαῦτα: τοιοῦτος — such, of such a kind; demonstr. pron./adj., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’such things’
τοὔνεκ: τοὔνεκα — for that reason, on that account (τοῦ ἕνεκα); adv., elided (τοὔνεκ’)
τοὶ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl.: ’they’; also relative: ’who’
τοῖον: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’in such a way’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun or pronoun: ’such a one as’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’) · also ’so’, qualifying an adj. · also neut. nom./acc. sg., agreeing with a neut. noun: τοῖον … ἔρνος (acc.), τοῖον … δόρυ (nom.) ’such a shoot, such a trunk’
τοῖσιν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’from/to them’
τρώεσσι: Τρῶες — the Trojans; masc. dat. pl.
τόδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. sg.
τόσσα: τόσος — so much, so many; epic τόσσος (doubled σ), neut. acc. pl.
τύμβον: τύμβος — burial mound, grave-mound; acc. sg.
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl. (μῆλα, τὰ … κατάκειτ’ ’the flocks, which lie’)
τὰς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. pl.: ‘them, those’ (referring to ships) · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the mules · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the cattle · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the fruits · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the nymphs and of the Sirens · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: fem. acc. pl. ’which’ (ἀπειλάων, τὰς … ἐπηπείλησε ’threats which he threatened’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’ · also article-like with a superlative or ordinal: ’the best’ (τὸν ἄριστον), ’the fourth’ (τὸν τέταρτον)
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’) · also demonstrative of a thing just named, before a preposition: ’it’ (τῷ δ’ ἐν ’and on it’, τῷ δ’ ὑπό ’and beneath it’)
φάτ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented, elided (φάτ’ = φάτο)
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φίλην: φίλος — dear, one’s own; fem. acc. sg.
φίλον: φίλος — dear, one’s own (with kin/body parts serves as a possessive); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: φίλον υἱόν ’dear son’ · also masc. acc. sg. predicative, agreeing with a pronoun: ’as a friend, welcome’ (φίλον ἐλθεῖν)
φίλων: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. gen. pl. (φίλοι ’kin, dear ones’) · also attributive with ἑταίρων: ’dear (companions)’ (φίλων … ἑταίρων)
φοίτων: φοιτάω — go to and fro, come repeatedly; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented, uncontracted (= Attic ἐφοίτων): ’were coming’
φρεσὶν: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. dat. pl.
φῆ: φημί — say, declare, assert; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφη): ’said, declared’
χαίρουσιν: χαίρω — rejoice, be glad; pres. 3 pl.
χερσίν: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., ν-movable
χερσὶ: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., epic -σί (= Attic χερσίν)
χλαῖνάν: χλαῖνα — a thick woollen cloak; fem. acc. sg.
χρήματ: χρῆμα — thing, matter; pl. χρήματα ’goods, property’; neut. acc. pl., elided (χρήματ’ = χρήματα)
χρὴ: χρή — it is necessary, it is right; impersonal verb + acc. and inf. · also + acc. of the person and gen. of the thing: ’there is need of’
ἀγορεύω: ἀγορεύω — speak, speak in assembly; pres. 1 sg.
ἀγχίμολον: ἀγχίμολος — coming near, close at hand; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’close by, hard upon’
ἀγόρευον: ἀγορεύω — speak, say, declare; impf. 3 pl.
ἀκλειῶς: ἀκλεής — without fame, inglorious; adv. ἀκλειῶς, epic spelling (= Attic ἀκλεῶς): ’without fame’
ἀλλήλους: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., masc. acc. pl.
ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’) · also + gen., ’about, concerning’ (ἀμφ’ Ἄρεος φιλότητος ’about the love of Ares’) · also with ὀστεόφιν, ’around’ (ἀμφ’ ὀστεόφιν θὶς ’a heap around the bones’)
ἀμφαδὸν: ἀμφαδόν — openly, in the open; adv.
ἀμφικαλύψας: ἀμφικαλύπτω — cover round about; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἀμφοτέροισι: ἀμφότερος — both (of two); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀμφοτέρῃσι: ἀμφότερος — both (of two); adj., fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι(ν) (= Attic -αις)
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἀμφὶ ... βάλλομεν = ἀμφιβάλλομεν ’we threw around, embraced’)
ἀμφὶς: ἀμφίς — apart, on both sides, around; adverb
ἀνέρες: ἀνήρ — man; masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἄνδρες)
ἀνηρείψαντο: ἀνερείπομαι — snatch up and carry away; aor. 3 pl., augment inside the compound (ἀν-ηρείψαντο, ε lengthened to η)
ἀνθρώπους: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; acc. pl.
ἀντιθέοις: ἀντίθεος — godlike, equal to the gods; adj., masc. dat. pl.
ἀπαμειβόμενος: ἀπαμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἀπεών: ἄπειμι — be away, be absent; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἀπών)
ἀποβάντες: ἀποβαίνω — step off, disembark; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.
ἀποσπένδων: ἀποσπένδω — pour out a libation; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἀπὸ: ἀπό — from, away from; + gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσει = ἀπολέσει ’will destroy’; ἀπὸ … δοθείη = ἀποδοθείη ’be given back’)
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg. · also ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἦγε): ’led’ · also ἄγω — lead; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead’ (μή μ’ ἄγε κεῖσ’ ’do not lead me there’)
ἄγοντες: ἄγω — lead, bring; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’bringing, leading’
ἄελλαι: ἄελλα — storm, squall, gust; fem. nom. pl.
ἄλλο: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄλλος: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. sg.
ἄνακτος: ἄναξ — lord, king, master; masc. gen. sg.
ἄναξ: ἄναξ — lord, master; masc. nom. sg. · also voc. sg. (same form), in address: ’lord!’ (κλῦθι, ἄναξ ’hear me, lord’)
ἄπιστος: ἄπιστος — disbelieving, not trusting; adj., masc. nom. sg., predicate
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄριστον: ἀγαθός — good; superl. ἄριστος, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’best’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with λαόν: ’best’ (λαὸν ἄριστον ’the best host’) · also masc. acc. sg. with the article, partitive: τὸν ἄριστον σιάλων ’the best of the hogs’
ἄσπετος: ἄσπετος — boundless, immense, unspeakable; fem. nom. sg. (two-ending adj.)
ἅμα: ἅμα — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἅρπυιαι: Ἅρπυιαι — the Harpies, snatching storm-winds personified as beings that carry people off without trace (from ἁρπάζω); nom. pl.
ἆ: ἆ — ah!, oh!; interjection of dismay or reproach
ἐγώ: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg. (accented ἐγώ before the enclitic τοι that follows) · also accented ἐγώ before the enclitic μιν that follows
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκέκλετο: κέλομαι — command, call to; reduplicated aor. 3 sg. mid., epic, + dat.: ’called to, bade’
ἐλεαίρων: ἐλεαίρω (epic by-form of ἐλεέω) — pity, have compassion on; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἐλεύσεσθαι: ἔρχομαι — go, come; fut. inf. mid.
ἐλθέμεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. inf., epic ἐλθέμεν (= Attic ἐλθεῖν): ’to come’
ἐμοί: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg., accented (non-enclitic emphatic): ’to me’
ἐμοὶ: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg.: ’to, for me’
ἐμοῖο: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ἐμὰ: ἐμός — my, mine; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)

ἐρχομένη: ἔρχομαι — come, go; pres. part. fem. nom. sg.
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσσυμένως: ἐσσυμένως — hastily, eagerly; adv. from the participle of σεύομαι ’rush’
ἐφαίνετο: φαίνομαι — appear, seem; impf. 3 sg.: ’was appearing, seemed’
ἐόντα: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc./neut. acc. sg., epic (= Attic ὄντα)
ἑτάροισι: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); dat. pl., epic -οισι
ἑτάροισιν: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν
ἑταίρους: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. acc. pl.
ἑταῖροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form), address: ’companions!’
ἔα: ἐάω — let be, allow, leave alone; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’leave alone!’ · also εἰμί — be; impf. 1 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν): ’I was’ (τοῖος ἔα ’such I was’)
ἔβαινον: βαίνω — go, step; impf. 3 pl. (or 1 sg.), augmented; in tmesis with ἀνά (ἀνά … ἔβαινον = ἀνέβαινον ’they mounted’)
ἔδοντες: ἔδω — eat (epic, = Attic ἐσθίω); pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’eating’
ἔδουσιν: ἐσθίω — eat; pres. 3 pl., from the epic present ἔδω (= Attic ἐσθίουσι)
ἔλθῃ: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. subj. 3 sg.: ’may come’
ἔλθῃσιν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσι(ν) (= Attic ἔλθῃ): ’may come’
ἔμ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (ἔμ’ = ἐμέ): ’me’
ἔνδον: ἔνδον — within, inside, at home; adv. (distinct from the by-form ἔνδοθι, also ’within’)
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔπι: ἐπί — on, upon, over; prep. + dat., placed after its noun with anastrophe: ἑοῖς ἔπι ’upon his own (possessions)’ · also + gen., postpositive with anastrophe, of direction: ’toward’ (νήσου ἔπι Ψυρίης ’toward the island of Psyria’) · also as adverb with no case expressed, intensifying repetition: ’besides, again’ (ἔπι δεύτερον αὖτις ’a second time, once more’) · also = ἔπεστι, accented on the first syllable when it stands for the verb: ’there is (upon)’ · also as preverb in tmesis, placed after its object: ἔπι … ὦρσεν = ἐπῶρσεν ’stirred up (against)’
ἔπλετο: πέλομαι — be, become, happen; aor. 3 sg. used with pres. force: ’is’ · also with ordinary past/aorist force: ’came to be, arose’ (τοῦτο νόημα ἔπλετο ’this thought has arisen’)
ἔργ: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl., elided (ἔργ’ = ἔργα)
ἔρξαν: ῥέζω — do, perform; aor. 3 pl., epic ἔρξαν (= Attic ἔδρασαν)
ἔφασκε: φημί — say, promise; impf. 3 sg., iterative -σκ-: ’kept saying, kept promising’
ἔχομεν: ἔχω — have, hold; pres./impf. 1 pl. (the form does not distinguish tense), past force in narration: ’we held (on)’
ἕκαστα: ἕκαστος — each, every; neut. acc. pl. used substantivally: ’each thing, everything’ · also adjectival, with a noun: ’each piece’ (ὅπλα ἕκαστα) · also neut. nom. pl. in apposition: ’each’ (πεντήκοντα δ’ ἕκαστα ’fifty to each’)
ἕλοντο: αἱρέω — take; aor. mid. 3 pl., unaugmented (= εἵλοντο): ’took (for themselves)’
ἕνεκ: ἕνεκα — because of, for the sake of; prep. + gen., elided (ἕνεκ’ = ἕνεκα)
ἠδέ: ἠδέ — and; epic conjunction, accented before an enclitic
ἠμὲν: ἠμέν — both (epic correlative, ἠμέν … ἠδέ ’both … and’); conj.
ἠνώγει: ἄνωγα (defective, perf. with pres. force) — command, bid, order; impf. 3 sg., augmented (ἠνώγει, beside unaugmented ἀνώγει elsewhere in this part), + inf.: ’was bidding’
ἠὲ: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ)
ἡμέτερον: ἡμέτερος — our, ours; neut. acc. sg.
ἢ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic ἠέ/ἤ) · also ’than’ after a comparative: κρεῖσσον … ἢ ὅτε ’better than when’ · also ’before’ after a verb of anticipating (ἔφθης … ἢ ἐγώ ’you got here before I did’) · also introducing the first alternative of an indirect question: ’whether’ (ἢ ἔτι … ἦέ τις ’whether still … or someone’) · also ’than’ after a verb of preferring: βουλοίμην … ἢ … ἀνάσσειν ’I would rather … than rule’
ἤγαγε: ἄγω — lead, bring; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’led, brought’
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤρατ: ἀείρω — lift, raise (Attic αἴρω); mid. win, gain for oneself; aor. mid. 3 sg., augmented, elided (ἤρατ’ = ἤρατο): ’won’; in sense the aorist of ἄρνυμαι ’win’, under which some lexica file it
ἥνδανε: ἁνδάνω — please, be pleasing to; impf. 3 sg., augmented (η- from the root’s original digamma, contracted; the same augment as the uncontracted ἑήνδανε in this part; unaugmented ἄνδανε); + dat.: ’was pleasing to’
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἦε: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ), spelled ἦε in ἦε καὶ οὐκί ’or not’
ἦλθεν: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’came’
ἦλθον: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. 3 pl.: ’they came’ · also aor. 1 sg. (the same ending serves both persons): ’I have come’
ἦμαρ: ἦμαρ — day (epic for ἡμέρα); neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἰδέσθαι: ὁράω — see; aor. mid. inf.: ‘to see’
ἵν: ἵνα — so that, in order that; conj., elided (ἵν’ = ἵνα) · also relative adverb of place, ’where’ (= Attic οὗ): τῶν ἐνὶ δήμῳ, ἵν’ οἴχεται ’among those of the land where he has gone’
ἵνα: ἵνα — so that, in order that; + subj. · also + opt. after a past tense · also relative ’where’ + indic.: ἵνα … καθεύδετον ’where the two are sleeping’
ὀΐομαι: ὀΐω — think, suppose; pres. 1 sg. mid., epic ὀΐομαι: ’I think’ (+ acc. and inf.)
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆος)
ὀδυσῆϊ: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. dat. sg., epic Ὀδυσῆϊ (single σ, diaeresis; = Ὀδυσσῆϊ, Attic Ὀδυσσεῖ)
ὀπίσσω: ὀπίσσω — behind; in Homer also ’hereafter, in time to come’; adv. · also ’back, home again’, of return (οἴκαδ’ ὀπίσσω ’back home’)
ὀφθαλμοῖσιν: ὀφθαλμός — eye; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’) · also distributive, masc. nom. sg.: ’the one’ (ὁ μὲν οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἱκάνει ’the one reaches the broad heaven’)
ὄλυμπον: Ὄλυμπος — Olympus, home of the gods; masc. acc. sg.
ὄφρ: ὄφρα (elided ὄφρ’) — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’as long as, while’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἔτι κεῖνος ἀνὴρ ἐπιδήμιος ἦεν ’as long as that man was still at home’) · also ’while’ + ἄν and subj. · also temporal ’until’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἵκετ’ Ἀρήτην ’until he came to Arete’) · also ’until’ + ἄν and subj. (ὄφρ’ ἂν ἵκηαι ’until you reach’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary verb: ’so that … might’ (ὄφρ’ … μένοιεν) · also temporal ’until’ + opt., of a hoped-for event (ὄφρ’ ἐξεμέσειεν ’until she should vomit out’)
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. (ὄφρα ... βάλε): marking the point an action ceases · also temporal + subj. with κε, correlative with τόφρα: ’as long as, until’ (ὄφρα κε κείνη τοῦτον ἔχῃ νόον ’for as long as she holds this purpose’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary-sequence verb: ὄφρα ... ἕλοις/ἵκοιο ’so that you might take/arrive’ · also temporal + indic., ’as long as’ (ὄφρα μὲν … ἦν ’so long as it was’)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅππως: ὅπως — how, in what way; epic ὅππως (double π metri gratia), with κε + subj. (or fut.): ’how you are to…’
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also with τις, an indirect interrogative: οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅς τις ’I know not who’ · also with τις, indefinite relative: ὅς τις … φάγοι ’whoever should eat’
ὅσ: ὅσος — as much/many as; relative correlative pron., neut. acc. pl., elided (ὅσ’ = ὅσα)
ὅσα: ὅσος — as much/many as; neut. acc. pl.: ’all that, as much as’ · also neut. nom. pl., subject: ὅσα φύλλα … γίγνεται ’as many leaves as come’
ὅτ: ὅτε (elided ὅτ’) — when; temporal conj., here + ἄν and subj. in a general/future clause · also + indic., of a single definite past event: ’when’ (ὅτ’ ἐν Ἄργεϊ ... ἵστασαν ’when they were mooring in Argos’) · also + opt., in a repeated past clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτ’ ἂψ ἄρχοιτο ’whenever he began again’) · also + subj. without ἄν, in a general clause: ὅτ’ … ἔχῃ ’whenever … holds’ · also in ὡς ὅτ’, ’as when (a minstrel does)’, the verb left unexpressed · also in ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ introducing a simile with a finite verb expressed: ’as when’ (ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ … ἁλιεὺς … προΐησι) · also causal + indic.: ’since, because’ (ὅτ’ οὐκ ἐθέλουσι δικαίως ’since they are not willing to act justly’)
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’) · also with the pres. indic., ’whereas, when’ (ὅτε τ’ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσ’ ἄνθρωποι ’whereas other men die only once’)
ὅττι: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; epic neut. nom./acc. sg. ὅττι (= Attic ὅ τι) · also with a superlative, ’as … as possible’ (ὅττι τάχιστα ’as quickly as possible’) · also in an indirect question, ’what’ (ὅττι ἑ κήδοι ’what was troubling him’) · also conj. ’that, because’, introducing a clause (ὅττι μιν ὣς ὑπέδεκτο ’that he had received him so’)
ὑφορβός: ὑφορβός — swineherd (ὑπό + φέρβω ’feed’); masc. nom. sg.
ὑψικόμοιο: ὑψίκομος — high-crowned, with lofty foliage; fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), with δρυός
ὑῶν: ὗς — pig, swine; masc./fem. gen. pl. (Attic ὑῶν)
ὕεσσιν: ὗς (σῦς) — swine; masc./fem. dat. pl., epic -εσσιν (= Attic ὑσί)
ὕλης: ὕλη — wood, forest, thicket; fem. gen. sg.
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’) · also ὡς + ἄν + opt., potential, ’as, in the way that, such as’ (ὡς οὐκ ἂν ἔλποιο ’such as you would not expect’) · also introducing a simile with the subj. and no ἄν: ’as when (a woman weeps)’ · also in an asseveration with fut. indic., ’as surely as’ (ὡς οὐκ ὀφθαλμόν γ’ ἰήσεται ’as surely as nothing will heal the eye’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. with a finite verb: ’how (dear) he is’ (ὡς ὅδε … φίλος … ἐστίν) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., of manner: ’as’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I shall say’) · also comparative ’like’, standing before its noun (ὡς νυκτερίς ’like a bat’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὥρη: ὥρα (Ionic ὥρη) — season, the right time, hour; fem. nom. sg. (Ionic η = Attic ᾱ): ’it is time (for)’
ὦκα: ὦκα — quickly, swiftly; adv., from ὠκύς
ὦρτο: ὄρνυμι — stir up, rouse; mid./intr. aor. 3 sg. ὦρτο, root aorist: ’arose’ (of a wind springing up) · also of a person: ’set out, started’ (ὦρτο πόλινδ’ ἴμεν ’set out to go to the city’)
ᾧ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc. dat. sg.: ’his own (son)’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which; masc. dat. sg. (δοίη δ’ ᾧ κ’ ἐθέλοι ’give her to whom he wished’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν, neut. dat. sg. (same form), agreeing with a neut. noun: πεδίοιο ... ᾧ ἔνι ... ’a plain in which is...’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν, neut. dat. sg., agreeing with ἄχεϊ: ’her own (grief)’
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥάκος: ῥάκος — rag, ragged cloth; neut. acc. sg.
ῥηϊδίως: ῥηΐδιος — easy; adv. ῥηϊδίως: ’easily, readily’, epic (= Attic ῥᾳδίως)
ῥωγαλέα: ῥωγαλέος — ragged, torn; neut. nom./acc. pl.
